title: The Badger's Tithe
story: Under the roots of the Old Oak, Thistledrum the Barrow Badger has hoarded 840 moonstone shards that rightfully belong to the woodcutters of Lantern Hollow. Mr 6 does not fight him; he offers a bargain the greedy badger cannot resist — a quarter of the hoard, kept honestly, instead of all of it, kept nervously. Thistledrum agrees, and the rest must be split evenly among the village's fourteen families.
question: Thistledrum keeps 25% of the 840 moonstone shards, and the rest is shared equally among 14 families. How many shards does each family receive?
solution: That leaves 840 - 210 = 630 shards for the village.
praise: Splitting the hoard among 14 was exactly right — the step that slipped past was taking out the badger's 25% before dividing.
hint: First figure out how many shards are actually left for the village after the badger's quarter is set aside.
victory: Thistledrum trundles off with his neat little pile, genuinely pleased for the first time in a century, and fourteen families light fourteen new lanterns. "A fair share," says Mr 6, "weighs less to carry."
imagePrompt: A stout grumbling badger in a moss cloak counting glowing moonstone shards among gnarled oak roots by lantern light, a small numeral-six knight chalking the division on a flat stone.
